doc.title: Dave Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

title: Founding and directing the Capital Focus Jazz Band
summary: A New Orleans-born businessman sponsored a youth trad band in Washington, D.C.; Dave has directed it for almost 19 years.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well yes. I got into education because, believe it or not, a gentleman in Washington, D.C., near where I live, years ago wanted to start up a youth traditional jazz band. He was a former resident of New Orleans and a friend of a lot of guys in the Preservation Hall band and so forth and he loved the music. He was a businessman and so he wanted to sponsor a youth group in town. So through the local jazz club they found me. I was starting to get into some educational things at that point in the schools, I would go out and do clinics and that kind of thing. But I wasn’t directing a band until that opportunity came along. So I took that on and it’s called The Capital Focus Jazz Band. It’s one of the very few traditional jazz bands on the east side of the U.S. And I’ve been directing them for about 19 years almost.
